Tournament mode is built and working. Typecheck, the 197 unit tests (including the project's source-rule tests) and Prettier all pass, and so does the full browser suite, 86 tests. That suite was 77 before and the 9 new ones are the tournament journeys. I did not commit anything.

I ran the browser tests on Node 22.23.4 and the system Chrome 153 (`PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=[machine-path]), not the README's named Node 26.12.1 and Chromium 156 combination. I ran `npm ci` first, which added the git-ignored `node_modules` and `.npm-cache`.

**How it behaves**
- **Opening it:** the Tournament button sits right after New Game and replaces the game screen. If a game is in progress it pauses, and Back to game returns to it with Resume.
- **Setup:**
  - The Players select offers 4 or 8, and the Player 1 to Player N inputs match it.
  - A blank name plays as its own label, such as "Player 3". Names are trimmed and limited to 24 characters. Duplicate names, ignoring case, are refused with "Player names must be different."
  - Start tournament, or Enter, starts it.
- **Turns:**
  - The screen shows "Now playing: NAME" and the match's deal code. The board only appears after Start turn.
  - When a game ends, Next turn appears. When a match ends, Next match appears.
  - The final match goes straight to "Champion: NAME", with Back to game and New tournament.
  - Leave tournament returns to setup and saves nothing.
- **Winning:**
  - Fewer moves wins.
  - A tie goes to the shorter time, then to the player listed first. You didn't specify a tie rule, so this is my choice; it's shown on screen and in the README.
- **Deals:**
  - Every match has its own deal, shared by its two players.
  - All deals use the grid size of the game you opened Tournament from, and tournament games never touch the saved bests.
- **Bracket:** each match shows its players, moves and time, and its winner, with "To be decided" until earlier matches finish.
- **Past tournaments:** finished tournaments are saved in browser storage (20 newest, under the key `neon-pairs.tournaments.v1`). They are listed on the setup screen with a View bracket button and survive a reload.
- **Export and Load:**
  - Export tournament and Load tournament work on every Tournament screen, using a "Tournament JSON" box. A finished tournament loaded this way is added to Past tournaments.
  - On the setup screen, Export saves the typed players with fresh deals as a tournament that has not started.
  - Game progress inside a turn isn't saved, so loading restarts that turn on the same deal. Invalid JSON leaves the screen unchanged.

**Changes to existing code and tests**
- **Game.tsx, Controls, control-labels, use-game:** wired in the button and the pause.
- **session.ts:** one new notice, for a game paused when opening Tournament.
- **BoardHelp.tsx:** the board help text moved here so both screens share it.
- **accessibility journey test:** the new button adds a Tab stop, so I added one Tab and one Shift+Tab to that test and a `tournament` entry to its fixture JSON.
- **spacing test:** I moved its spacing-scale checker into `tests/spacing-scale.ts` so the tournament tests can reuse it.
- **README:** a new Tournament section.

I followed the project rules as the source tests encode them: files under 200 lines, no type escapes, every export imported somewhere, yes/no checks named `is` or `has`, and spacing on the existing scale.

The new code is in `src/game/tournament/`, with unit tests beside it. The new browser tests are `tests/tournament.e2e.test.ts` and `tests/tournament-transfer.e2e.test.ts`, with a helper in `tests/tournament-fixture.ts`.

finalMessage:
Tournament mode is built, with the docs updated to match. Typecheck passes and unit tests pass (27 files, 180 tests). The full browser suite, run once before two small test edits, passed 92 of 93. The one failure was the existing keyboard journey, which needed an extra Tab for the new button. I updated it and reran it with the tournament test, and both passed. Nothing was committed.

The browser tests ran on Chrome 153 and Node 22 (set through `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`), not the README's named Chromium 156 / Node 26 combination. So the README's tested-versions record is untouched and the named-combination run is not done. `prettier --check` passes on `src`, `tests`, `scripts` and `art`. It fails on `docs/` (about 210 files) before and after my changes, so I did not reformat docs.

**How the project rules shaped it**
- **Name checks:** the CLI isn't installed, so I followed the loader by hand and read the competition, interface, persistence, sharing, architecture and writing docs. Names are trimmed, collapsed and NFC-normalized. They must be 2 to 20 code points ("Use 2 to 20 characters.") and unique ignoring case ("Each name must be different.").
- **Bracket rules:** pairings are 1v4, 2v3 for four players and 1v8, 4v5, 3v6, 2v7 for eight. Rounds read "Round: Quarterfinal/Semifinal/Final" on 4x4, 6x6 and 8x8 boards. Every match gets a different full board code, drawn through `freshBoardCode`. Ties go to fewer moves, then less active time in milliseconds, then the higher seed.
- **Results table:** the bracket is a `<table>` with a caption and `th scope="col"` headers. A winner shows "(winner)" after the name.
- **Screens and dialog:** each screen's h2 has `tabindex="-1"` and takes focus. Leave tournament opens a native `<dialog>` with Keep playing (focused) and Leave, and Escape keeps playing.
- **Live region:** there is still only one on the page. "Now playing: NAME", validation errors and load results all go through it.
- **Saved list:** `np3:tournaments` holds `{"items":[…],"v":3}` and keeps the newest 10. Corrupt data reads as empty. Blocked storage shows "Progress won't be saved on this device."
- **Export format:** the JSON has `format: "neon-pairs/tournament"` and `version: 1`, with keys in alphabetical order at every level. Load rejects the first unknown field as "Unknown field: NAME." and anything else as "Invalid tournament."
- **Isolation:** tournament games run in their own session, so saved size and best moves never change. A browser test confirms this with seeded preferences.
- **Layout rules:** controls are at least 44x44 at 390px wide and spacing stays on the scale, both checked in browser tests. Files stay under 200 lines, rules are in `src/game/tournament/rules.ts` (React-free) with unit tests beside them, and new exports are all imported.

**Choices of mine you may want to change**
- The Tournament button sits directly after New Game, so the bar reads New Game, Tournament, Restart.
- After the Final's second game the screen goes straight to "Champion: NAME" with Back to game; there is no Next match button for the last match.
- Opening Tournament while a solo game is running keeps that game and stops its clock until Back to game. This needed a small `suspended` option on the session clock.
- Export on the setup screen exports the entry form as a draft with no matches. Load accepts that draft and refills the form.
- Load tournament replaces the current tournament without asking, like Load snapshot. Only Leave tournament asks first.
- A tournament loaded from JSON is shown but not added to Past tournaments. Only one played to its end here is.
- A running tournament is not saved across a reload. Export it first to keep it.

**Changes outside the tournament folder**
- `Game.tsx` now switches between the solo page and the tournament screen.
- Two small components were pulled out so both screens share them: `status/GameResult.tsx` (the one live region) and `board/BoardHelp.tsx`.
- `GameStatus` takes an optional `showBest`, and the tournament turn hides Best.
- The spacing helper moved to `tests/spacing-audit.ts` so tournament screens get the same audit.
- Docs: I added `docs/competition/competition-tournament.md` and edited about 20 existing pages. I left the spec version at 2.2 and did not touch history or ADR pages.

New code is in `src/game/tournament/`. Tests are `src/game/tournament/*.test.ts` plus `tests/tournament*.e2e.test.ts` (including `tests/tournament-fixture.ts`).

finalMessage:
Tournament mode is in and working in the project folder. `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass (26 files, 177 tests). `npm run test:e2e` passes 84 of 84 (77 existing plus 7 new). The e2e run used the sandbox's Chromium 1243 through `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE`, not the README's named combination, and under Node 22 rather than Node 24+[machine-path] so none of it counts as named-combination evidence. Nothing is committed, and I started no dev servers.

## What you get
- **Opening it:** a "Tournament" button sits right after New Game and replaces the main area with the Tournament screen. Focus lands on its `h2`.
- **Setup:** a Players select (4 or 8), inputs labelled "Player 1" to "Player N", and "Start tournament".
- **Play:** "Now playing: NAME", "Start turn", "Next turn", "Next match" and "Leave tournament" work as you described. The board is not drawn before Start turn and is removed on Next turn / Next match, so the second player never sees the deal.
- **Results:** the bracket is a table with a caption, `th scope="col"` headers, one row per player per match, plus moves, time and winner. The final shows "Champion: NAME" and "Back to game".
- **Records:** finished tournaments go into "Past tournaments" on the setup screen and survive reload.
- **Exchange:** "Tournament JSON" box with "Export tournament" and "Load tournament" on every screen, including setup.

## Project rules followed that you did not spell out
- **Pairing and rounds:** seeds follow entry order. Four players meet 1v4 then 2v3. Eight meet 1v8, 4v5, 3v6, 2v7. Rounds are Quarterfinal on 4x4, Semifinal on 6x6, Final on 8x8, shown as "Round: NAME". Four players have no quarterfinal.
- **Deals:** both players of a match play one board code, and every match in a tournament gets a different full code. All codes are chosen at start, using only the existing fresh-code helper.
- **Tie-breaks:** fewer moves win, then lower active time, then the higher seed. Time is compared as whole milliseconds recorded when the game ends, never from displayed text.
- **Preferences:** tournament games run in their own session. The saved size and best scores are never touched, and the e2e test checks the stored preferences are byte-identical afterwards.
- **Names:** trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed, NFC. Length is 2 to 20 code points, giving "Use 2 to 20 characters." Case-insensitive repeats give "Each name must be different." The inputs have no `maxlength`, so the check sees what was typed.
- **Leave:** "Leave tournament" opens a native dialog with "Keep playing" and "Leave". Keep playing takes focus and Escape keeps playing.
- **Live region:** there is still exactly one, in `Game.tsx`. "Now playing", name and load errors, turn results and match verdicts go through it. The Tournament screen adds no second one.
- **Storage:** the past list is stored under `np3:tournaments` as `{"v":3,"items":[...]}` and keeps the newest 10. A value that cannot be read counts as empty and is left alone. A blocked store shows "Progress won't be saved on this device." by the past list.
- **Export format:** the document has `format: "neon-pairs/tournament"` and a whole-number `version`, with keys alphabetical at every level. A field the format does not define gives "Unknown field: NAME." Other problems give "Invalid tournament." Load checks the whole text first and keeps the current state on failure.
- **Layout:** every new control is at least 44px at a 390px viewport with no sideways scroll, and the e2e suite checks it.
- **Code placement:** rules are in `src/game/tournament/rules.ts` with tests beside it. No new dependencies, all TypeScript files are 200 lines or fewer, and the source audits pass.

## Choices to review
- **Existing test changed.** Adding a button to the deal bar changes the Tab count in the accessibility journey, so I updated `tests/accessibility.e2e.test.ts`: 3 Tabs from New Game to the board, 4 Shift+Tabs back.
- **Leave returns to setup.** "Leave tournament" goes back to the setup screen, not to the game. "Back to game" also exists on the setup screen.
- **Past list is setup-only.** "Past tournaments" shows on the setup screen only, so the finished screen has a single table.
- **Setup export is a draft.** Export on setup writes a "draft" document with no matches. Loading it fills the form, and its names are still validated at Start.
- **Loaded tournaments are not saved.** A loaded tournament is untrusted, so loading one never adds it to the past list.
- **Game clock keeps running.** The solo game stays in memory while the Tournament screen is open, and its clock keeps running because nothing in the spec pauses it. Say if you want that changed.
- **Docs, no version bump.** I added `docs/competition/tournament.md` (K01 to K20) and updated the README map, controls (C15), acceptance, source layout, persistence overview and the competition, dialog, focus, tables, name and announcement pages that said these features did not exist. I did not bump the spec version.
- **Formatting.** `prettier --check` still fails on many existing docs that I did not touch; everything I added or edited in `src`, `tests`, `README.md` and `tournament.md` passes.

Main files: `src/game/tournament/` (rules, names, format, storage, deals, flow, controller and the screen components), `src/game/Game.tsx`, `src/game/controls/Controls.tsx`, `tests/tournament*.ts`.

**What a player sees**
- The Tournament button sits right after New Game and opens a screen with a Players select (4 or 8), Player 1–N inputs and Start tournament.
- Each match shows "Round: NAME" and "Now playing: NAME". Start turn begins a game. Next turn or Next match appears when a game or match ends, and Leave tournament asks first.

- The bracket is a table with each match's players, moves, time and board code, with "(winner)" after the winner's name.
- The Tournament JSON box with Export tournament and Load tournament is on every Tournament screen.

**Project rules applied**
- **Pairing and boards:** seeds come from entry order. Eight players open 1v8, 4v5, 3v6, 2v7; four players open 1v4, 2v3. Quarterfinals are 4x4, semifinals 6x6, the final 8x8. Every match gets its own board code, drawn through the project's one allowed random source, and both players of a match play that code.
- **Winner:** fewer moves, then lower active time in whole milliseconds, then the higher seed.
- **Names:** trimmed, whitespace-collapsed and NFC-normalised. 2–20 code points ("Use 2 to 20 characters."), no case-insensitive repeats ("Each name must be different.").
- **Live region:** "Now playing" and "Champion" go through the page's single live region.

- **Saved records:** stored as `np3:tournaments` with `{"v":3,"items":[…]}`, newest 10 kept. A blocked store keeps the list in memory and shows "Progress won't be saved on this device."
